title: I Took the Perfume-Still Booking to the Intern Who Palmed My Numbered Pipettes

parts.text: I stepped into the still room at 1:06 p.m. and intern Noor was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE STILL. NINETY MINUTES. PIPETTES STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was twenty-seven, studio secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered pipettes. Noor shrugged. "Interns are the still." I photographed the board, the booking, and her leftover accords on my numbered pipettes. Then I asked for the still log. At 1:14 the desk pinged why Noor's name was on my accords. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The desk can see Noor's leftover accords on my numbered pipettes.

social.video_title: She palmed my numbered perfume pipettes on my still — Part 1/2
social.description: Still room, leftover accords, a ninety-minute clock she posted. I logged the pipettes. Would you have asked for the still log?

parts.text: Noor called it blending until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the accord still. The pipettes went back to my numbered booking. Noor ran a slot of her own and told the next intern atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: INTERNS ARE NOT THE STILL. I keep my pipettes in a labeled rack. Noor brown-bags her blending. The still room finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Interns are not the still — Part 2/2
social.description: Still log, numbered pipettes, and a second line on the board. Was blending ever my accords?
